bio: Hi! I am a student from Northern Virginia, studying Data Science and Computer Science at UC Berkeley. I'm interested in AI alignment/safety, robotics, machine learning, and the role of technology in society. Outside of classes, I teach web development as part of the Hackathons @ Berkeley Club and am a member of ACE Coaches, and teach students at the YMCA in San Francisco Chinatown. In addition, I play Quizbowl, transcribe music, build PCs, read (mainly sci-fi), and spend time with friends and family.

contact.note: Open to internships, research, and collaborations, especially anything in AI alignment and safety. Email is the fasest way to reach me.

jobs.title: Data Discovery Research Intern
points: Developing and testing approaches to segmenting cuneiform signs on photographed tablets, the current bottleneck in TokenWorks' cuneiform OCR pipeline.
Using a U-Net with a ResNet-34 backbone to pick out high-level features on tablet images and detect lines of cuneiform.

jobs.title: AI Prompt Engineer Intern
points: Supported the Border Enforcement Applications for Government Leading-Edge Information Technology program, delivering software for U.S. Customs and Border Protection.
Designed, tested, and optimized LLM prompts so outputs stayed reliable and complex requirements translated into working AI interactions.

jobs.title: IT Specialist
points: Building a medical software system that centralizes appointment scheduling for patients and clinic staff, with speech-to-text transcription to speed up clinical note-taking, all within HIPAA compliance.
Running hands-on testing sessions with clinic employees to make sure every feature is usable by the people who depend on it.

jobs.title: AI Engineer
points: Engineered a proof-of-concept AI for a reading app that builds and updates a symbolic "mental model" of the reader as they go.
Built demos that watch ongoing reader interactions to predict their next questions and deductions, then wired LLMs in to turn the idea into a working prototype.

jobs.title: Robotics Research Intern
jobs.org: Prof. Gregory Stein's Lab · George Mason University
points: Researched robotic decision-making under limited information by building an interface between the AI model and its environment, then tested state-of-the-art planning models in both simulated and real settings.
Developed symbolic interior environments, from apartments to office spaces, for planning algorithms to navigate.

jobs.title: Student Research Apprentice
points: Collected and processed 200k+ state-level electrical outage reports to train a weather-outage prediction model.
Improved LSTM, TCN, and Transformer models that forecast wind speeds around wind farms a day ahead, cutting error by 20%.
Presented findings to lab researchers and contributed analyses to model-training discussions.

projects.name: Luminate
projects.desc: Luminate is an agentic fact-checking and AI-content detection platform for social media, grown from a 2026 Innovation Intelligence Hackathon prototype into a real verification tool. A multi-agent backend uses retrieval-augmented generation over a PostgreSQL vector database to evaluate claims, cross-reference sources, and run multi-step verification on its own, while a React web app and a companion browser extension bring the analysis into the page you are reading.

projects.name: Cal Hacks 13.0 Hardware Checkout
projects.desc: This projecy involved analysis of request and inventory data from the hardware lending desk at Cal Hacks 13.0, done to improve staffing, stocking, and the hacker experience at future Hackathons @ Berkeley events. Demand peaked in the first hour, four categories were oversubscribed with boards requested at nearly three times available stock, and bulk components sat heavily overstocked, so the recommendation was to shift budget toward boards, kits, peripherals, and sensors.

projects.name: QBVReader
projects.desc: QBVReader is a Quizbowl practice app that recreates tournament reading conditions, tracks performance, and shows players their strengths and weaknesses by category. It serves 1,900+ users and 190+ high school and college teams nationwide, including Dartmouth, Virginia Tech, and Purdue, and improves accessibility for players with hearing or speaking disabilities.

projects.name: Human Decision-Making Through Chess
projects.desc: This was a research project on whether neural networks can model human decision-making rather than just optimal play, using aggressive chess styles as the test case. Two networks trained with TensorFlow, a convolutional one and a standard one, read the board state to score aggression and move quality from features like king safety, mobility, and pawn structure. The aggression classifier reached 99.65% accuracy and exposed a real trade-off between aggression and move quality, which is exactly the kind of gap between what a model optimizes and what we actually want that draws me to alignment work.

projects.name: Pathway Paver
projects.desc: Pathway Paver is a grid-based puzzle game where players guide cars to their colour-matched destinations by placing road tiles. Each level adds limited resources, turn constraints, and obstacles such as trees, so routes have to be planned to avoid collisions and dead ends. Nicholas Lee and I built it for the 2025 McLean Hackathon, where it took first place.

projects.name: AI Adoption in the US Military
projects.desc: I am currently working on an ongoing research paper on the integration of AI into Defense Department systems in the context of the Iran War. It looks at the technical implementation, how Defense employees understand and govern the systems internally, and the consequences for decision-making inside the military and for the actions it takes outside it.

hobbies.desc: I have been playing [Quizbowl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quiz_bowl) since the start of middle school, specializing history, geography, and mythology. I most recently competed in [ACF Fall 2026](https://hsquizbowl.org/db/tournaments/10688/stats/all_games/), where my team won 1st place.
I transcribe music in my spare time. You can find some of my work [here](https://onlinesequencer.net/members/179356) at Online Sequencer.
I started building PCs during COVID, and have continued since then, mainly at the request of friends or family.

I read a lot, mainly science fiction and biographies. Favorite books include Dune by Frank Herbert, Stand on Zanzibar By John Brunner, House of Huawei, and The Philosopher in the Valley by Michael Steinberger.

I'm a Director at Hackathons @ Berkeley on the Cubstart, where I teach web development to a class of 50+ UC Berkeley students. In addition, I have worked on the course website and grading software for webpage homework submission.
I volunteer at the YMCA in San Francisco Chinatown as part of the Ace Coaches UC Berkeley club, teaching mainly math and english.
